column3: Usage
column4: ExampleZh
column5: ExampleEn

column3: come/go/return from a place; 从 goes first and the verb comes at the end and cannot be omitted
column4: 她是从北京来的留学生。
column5: She is an international student from Beijing.

column3: very much adj.; extremely adj.
column4: 她是从北京来的留学生，英文说得好极了。
column5: She is an international student from Beijing, and she speaks English extremely well.

column3: a choice-type question that produces the effect of the English word "if"
column4: 她问我有没有中文名字。
column5: She asked me if I had a Chinese name.

column3: because ... therefore ...; used in both written and spoken Chinese to make logic clearer and more persuasive
column4: 因为爸爸妈妈是在纽约谈恋爱的，所以我们给你起了这个名字。
column5: Because Mom and Dad fell in love in New York, we gave you this name.

column3: have to, need to; structure: (subject/time/location) + 得 + verb; 学会 = to master something (V + resultative complement)
column4: 狗狗得学会控制自己。
column5: The doggie has to learn how to control itself.

column3: put thought or effort into ...; often used as "somebody 在 something 上花心思"
column4: 中国父母常常在每个名字上花很多心思。
column5: Chinese parents often put a lot of thought into each name.

column3: emphasizes a negation, usually negating a previous statement or assumption
column4: 起个完美的名字并不容易。
column5: It's not easy to have a perfect name.

column3: base on; according to; can begin a sentence or be used as "somebody + 根据 + something + verb + noun"
column4: 根据2019年全国姓名报告，全中国有差不多三十万人叫张伟呢！
column5: According to the 2019 national name report, there are almost 300,000 people in China named Zhang Wei!

column3: used literally like "up", figuratively as a direction complement for a spontaneous action or state that has started, or with perception verbs (看/听/闻/摸) to express how the subject seems
column4: Alex听起来像 "爱你克死"。
column5: Alex sounds like "Àinǐkèsǐ".

column3: although ... yet ...
column4: 虽然她移民来美国已经快二十五年了,但是还保留了很多中国人的生活习惯。
column5: Although she has immigrated to the United States for almost 25 years, she still retains many Chinese habits.

column3: whoever, whatever, whenever, etc.
column4: 中国人觉得爸爸是哪儿人,孩子就是哪儿人。
column5: Chinese people think that wherever the father is from, the child is from.

column3: structure to mark time, place, manner, or initiator of a known past action
column4: 我爸爸是从北京来的。
column5: My father is from Beijing.

column1: A 跟 B 一样 + verb/adj.
column3: the same as ...
column4: 我小时候也跟你一样 (不清楚自己是哪儿人)。
column5: I was just like you when I was a kid (not very clear about where I was from).

column3: only then; not until
column4: 后来才想清楚我是中国人,也是美国人,我就是华裔美国人啊。
column5: Not until later did I figure out that I am both Chinese and American. I am Chinese American.

column3: doing V1 and V2 at the same time; carrying out V2 in the manner of V1
column4: 我拉着行李箱在芝加哥机场排队过安检。
column5: I am in line for the security check with my luggage at the Chicago airport.

column3: do an action to a definite object, emphasizing the effect on it
column4: 我赶紧把护照和机票递给安检人员。
column5: I quickly gave my passport and tickets to the security check personnel.

column3: in order to ...
column4: 为了快点儿过安检,我给了他他想要的答案。
column5: In order to pass the security check quickly, I gave him the answer that he wanted.

column3: relative clause structure (the Noun that someone V's)
column4: 我给了他他想要的答案。
column5: I gave him the answer that he wanted.

column3: as far as someone is concerned; in someone's view
column4: 在他看来,谁可以算是 "美国人"?
column5: In his view, who can be considered to be "American"?

column3: to think something mistakenly
column4: 她是你妈妈? 我以为她是你姐姐呢!
column5: Is she your mother? I thought she was your sister!

column3: a bit adj. (implies something negative); in speech 一 is often dropped, leaving 有点, pronounced 有点儿 in northern China
column4: 爸爸的普通话和妈妈的有一点不一样。
column5: My father's Mandarin is a little different from my mother's.

column3: can/cannot verb (potential complement); indicates whether or not an action is possible
column4: 我一句都听不懂。
column5: I cannot understand even one sentence.

column3: verb back and forth, a reciprocal action; the verb should be at least two syllables
column4: 两个说不同方言的人常常互相听不懂。
column5: Two people who speak different dialects often can't understand each other.

column3: extremely adj.; usually implies the situation is serious, but can also be positive (e.g. 高兴得不得了)
column4: 中国的方言多得不得了!
column5: There are so many dialects in China!

column3: turns an adjective into an adverb, like the English suffix '-ly'; a one-syllable adjective is repeated (e.g. 慢慢地)
column4: 我在里面听到妈妈大声地跟朋友说："你要死掉了。"
column5: I was inside the room and heard my mother say loudly to her friends, "You are going to die."

column3: even more ...; adds '-er' to an adjective, and can be used with 比 (A 比 B + 更 + Adj.), adding the meaning of 'even more'
column4: 我们觉得用英文更清楚、更方便。
column5: We find it even clearer and more convenient to use English.

column3: on the one hand, on the other hand; used to talk about various aspects of a situation, which can be similar or opposed; 又, 也, or 还 is sometimes added after 另一方面 for emphasis
column4: 一方面,当时外公家没有暖气,冷得不得了。另一方面,妈妈一家人在一起的时候都说上海话。
column5: On the one hand, there was no heating at my grandpa's house, and it was terribly cold. On the other hand, my mother's family spoke Shanghainese when they were together.

column1: 一 + measure word + (noun) + 都/也 + 不/没 + verb
column3: not even one; indicates that someone did not do something at all
column4: 我一句都听不懂。
column5: I cannot understand even one sentence.

column3: how well an action is done; 得 + adj is a degree complement providing additional information of degree for the verb
column4: 妈妈的家人很关心我吃得好不好,玩得高兴不高兴。
column5: My mother's family was very concerned about whether I ate well and whether I had fun or not.

column3: a structure unique to Chinese; once the topic (usually a person or thing) is raised, the rest of the sentence comments on it; the topic operates on a discourse level beyond the confines of a single sentence
column4: 上海话我还是听不懂。
column5: Shanghainese, I still cannot understand.

column3: according to someone's statement/ways of saying a thing
column4: 照官方说法,现在有十大方言。
column5: According to the official statement, there are now ten regional varieties of Chinese.

column3: no matter . . . (what follows 无论 should be a question, not a statement)
column4: 南方方言和北方方言,无论是发音、词汇还是语法都不一样。
column5: No matter if it is pronunciation, vocabulary, or grammar, the language varieties in the southern regions and the northern regions are different.

column3: not at all; absolutely not (cannot be followed by an affirmative statement)
column4: 如果他和妈妈两个人都用方言说话,就会像“鸡同鸭讲”,根本听不懂。
column5: If he and his mother both spoke in language varieties, they would be like how 'a chicken talks to a duck', and they would not understand each other at all.

column3: to indicate that the action lasted for a long time, often followed by 也/都/还没有 + resultative verb
column4: 一个东北人听到后马上跳到河里帮她找,可是找了半天都没有找到孩子。
column5: After hearing that, a northeasterner immediately jumped into the river to help her but still could not find the child after searching for a long time.

column3: (mistakenly) read/see/regard/call something as something else
column4: 四川人都把“鞋子”读成“孩子”。
column5: Sichuan people pronounce 'xiezi' as 'haizi'.

column3: Then how adjective it would be
column4: 如果没有了方言,那该多无聊啊!
column5: If there were no language varieties, then how boring it would be!

column1: 对 + something + 有兴趣/感兴趣
column3: be interested in something (when used with a person, it means interested as a study subject, not romantically)
column4: 他对语言学也很有兴趣。
column5: He is interested in linguistics.

column3: Not only . . . but also . . . (both parts in the same realm; the focus is the second part)
column4: 汉语拼音不但提高了中国人的读写能力,而且让外国人学习中文变得容易多了。
column5: The Pinyin system not only improves Chinese people's reading and writing abilities but also makes learning Chinese for foreigners much easier.

column3: in addition . . . (often placed at the beginning of the sentence, which often also has 也)
column4: 另外,拼音也方便了人们在电脑或手机上打字。
column5: Besides, Pinyin also makes typing on computers and cell phones more convenient.

column3: have done something before (focuses on past experience that impacts current experience)
column4: 你听过周有光这个人吗?
column5: Have you heard of this person, Zhou Youguang?

column3: however (indicates a surprise element; 却 goes before the verb, not at the beginning of the sentence)
column4: 他原来是银行家。50岁以后,他却成了一位语言文字学家。
column5: He originally was a banker. After turning 50 years old, he, however, has become a linguist.

column1: Subject + (已经) + Duration + 没 + Verb + 了
column3: have not done something for a period of time (已经 can be omitted)
column4: 你已经一个月没跟爸爸妈妈视频聊天了。
column5: You haven't had a video chat with Mom and Dad for a month.

column3: besides / in addition to ... (with 都 it means "except")
column4: 除了上课以外,我也参加了两个社团,另外还想找实习。
column5: Besides attending classes, I also joined two clubs, and I also want to find an internship.

column1: Subject + 一点(儿) + 也/都 + 不 + Adj./Verb Phrase
column3: not ... at all
column4: 你们俩一点都不关心父母!
column5: You two don't care about your parents at all!

column3: quite / rather / pretty (adjective); common in spoken Chinese
column4: 她跟哥哥很谈得来。看起来挺有气质的。
column5: She gets along well with her brother and looks pretty cultivated.

column3: be able to talk to; get along well with
column4: 她跟哥哥很谈得来。
column5: She gets along well with her brother.

column3: intensifies an adjective with an unpleasant connotation ("... to death")
column4: 我真的急死了。
column5: I am really worried to death.

column3: lower/higher than ...; 于 follows an adjective to indicate comparison, with the same meaning as 比
column4: 成绩不可以低于A。
column5: Grades cannot be lower than A.

column3: A is not as adj. as B
column4: 我的父母没有蔡美儿那么严格。
column5: My parents are not as strict as Amy Chua.

column2: ná A gēn B zuò bǐjiào
column3: compare A with B
column4: 父母喜欢拿我跟"别人家的孩子"做比较。
column5: My parents like to compare me with "other people's kids".

column3: as soon as / once / whenever action 1 happens, action 2 happens
column4: 王阿姨的儿子一毕业就拿到了年薪10万美金的工作。
column5: Upon graduation, Aunt Wang's son got a job with an annual salary of 100,000 U.S. dollars.

column3: make sacrifice for ... / the sacrifice made for ...
column4: 另一些压力来自于父母为我的教育做出的牺牲。
column5: Other pressures came from the sacrifices my parents made for my education.

column3: under the pressure of ...
column4: 在这些压力下,父母的关心和爱却成了我的负担。
column5: Under these pressures, the care and love of my parents became my burden.

column3: both . . . and . . . (the two highlighted traits should both be positive or both negative)
column4: 中文学校的功课又多又难。
column5: The homework in Chinese school is so many and difficult.

column3: more and more adj./stative verb over time
column4: 我越来越讨厌这种生活,特别是牺牲星期六的时间去中文学校。
column5: I hate this kind of life more and more, especially when I sacrifice Saturdays to go to Chinese school.

column3: the more . . . the more (verbs typically follow the first yue, adjectives/emotion verbs follow the second)
column4: 大家越吃越奇怪,吃起来像鸡肉,一点也不像牛肉。
column5: The more everyone eats it, the stranger they feel. It tastes like chicken, not like beef at all.

column3: to/for someone (feeling/opinion based on personal experience)
column4: 对我来说,学中文并不只是为了满足大学的语言要求,也是为了和妈妈在中国的家人交流。
column5: For me, learning Chinese is not only to meet the language requirements of universities but also to communicate with my mother's family in China.

column3: more than . . . it is also . . . (并 strengthens the tone)
column4: 我家的狗狗不只是宠物,也是我的家人。
column5: Our doggie is more than a pet; it is also my family.

column3: ba-structure describing the disposal of an object and the result the action leads to
column4: 如果我把中文学好,将来还可以教我的小孩。
column5: If I learn Chinese well, I can teach my children in the future.

column3: from . . . to . . .
column4: 我们从星期一到星期五都有中文课。
column5: We have Chinese classes from Mondays to Fridays.

column3: suffer from . . . or is received . . . (used in positive or negative situations; the thing received must be abstract)
column4: 《排华法案》以后,中国移民受到很严重的歧视。
column5: After the Chinese Exclusion Act, Chinese immigrants suffered from discrimination.

column3: do something with someone (the verb goes after 'with someone')
column4: 美国人想跟中国做生意。
column5: Americans would like to do business with China.

column3: Therefore . . . (summarizes the previous statement; placed at the beginning)
column4: 因此,戈鲲化的故事告诉我们,美国中文教育的发展跟政治和经济有直接的关系。
column5: Therefore, from the story of Ge Kunhua, we know that the development of Chinese education in the United States is directly related to politics and economy.

column1: A 跟 B 有 …… 的关系
column2: A gēn B yǒu ... de guānxi
column3: A is related to B / A has something to do with B
column4: 美国中文教育的发展跟政治和经济有直接的关系。
column5: The development of Chinese language education in the U.S. is directly related to politics and economy.

column3: if it's not . . . it's . . .; to describe a situation as being one of only two possibilities
column4: 在学校午餐很简单,不是三明治就是汉堡。
column5: Lunch at school is very simple, either sandwiches or hamburgers.

column3: be unable to endure; cannot stand/bear; "不+了" is the negative complement form of "得+了", used with many verbs and some adjectives
column4: 我中午在学校吃了几天汉堡就受不了。
column5: I can't stand eating hamburgers at school for a few days at noon.

column3: an adverb indicating "have no choice but to", where the option is not liked by the speaker
column4: 后来只好自己带中餐去学校吃。
column5: Later, I had to bring my own Chinese food to school.

column3: on the contrary; but actually; used in conversation to indicate an opposite opinion or something not expected
column4: 我倒是觉得汉堡挺好吃的,也很方便。
column5: I think hamburgers are delicious and convenient.

column3: no wonder; used to convey the speaker's newfound understanding that something is unsurprising
column4: 原来是这样! 难怪人家说没有。
column5: That's it! No wonder they say no.

column3: under the circumstance or "in this case"; often used at the beginning of a sentence to refer to a previously mentioned circumstance or situation
column4: 在这种情况下,很多华人声称自己是在美国出生的,是美国公民,但他们的出生记录被烧毁了。
column5: Under such circumstances, many Chinese claimed to be born in the United States and American citizens, but their birth records were burned.

column3: verb + resultative complement; the complement can be an adjective (好、晚、光、干净) or a monosyllabic verb (完、会、到) indicating the result of an action
column4: 市政厅着火,烧毁了大量移民的出生记录。
column5: The city hall caught fire and destroyed the birth records of a large number of immigrants.

column3: in this way; thus; used at the start of a sentence or clause to indicate that only in this way can or will something happen
column4: 这样,他们才可以得到移民名额。
column5: In this way, they could get the immigrant quota.

column3: with the identity of; as . . .; used as "someone 以……身份 + verb" to emphasize the identity someone has when doing something
column4: 从1910年到1940年,还是有很多的华人以"纸儿女"的身份进入了美国。
column5: From 1910 to 1940, many Chinese entered the United States as "paper sons and paper daughters".

column3: verb toward the direction
column4: 秦朝版图往南到今天的广东和广西省,往西南到今天的四川省。
column5: The territory of the Qin Dynasty went south to today's Guangdong and Guangxi provinces, and southwest to today's Sichuan Province.

column3: verb gradually (an uncontrollable change, often used with 变 or a verb + resultative)
column4: 用长城保护中国的想法也渐渐地变了。
column5: The idea of using the Great Wall to protect China has gradually changed.

column3: every . . .
column4: 在美国,每个州都有一个州府。在中国,每个省都有一个省会。
column5: In America, every state has a state capital. In China, every province has a provincial capital.

column1: 后来 vs. 以后 vs. 然后
column3: 后来 = later (past events only); 以后 = in the future (future events only); 然后 = and then (conjunction, often in 先 …… 然后 …… for sequence)
column4: 商周时代中国的版图很小。后来中国的版图经过了很多朝代,就越来越大了。
column5: China in the Shang and Zhou eras had a very small territory. Later, China's territory went through many dynasties, and it became bigger and bigger.

column3: is located in (place); frequently used in written language
column4: 四川省位于中国的西南部。
column5: Sichuan Province is located in the southwestern part of China.

column3: S is composed of (what follows 由 are the elements of the subject)
column4: 四川省由四川盆地和高原山地两大部分组成的。
column5: Sichuan Province is composed of two geographic parts, the Sichuan basin and the plateau.

column3: one of (noun/number); the number after 之 can be fluid, e.g. 三分之二 = 2/3
column4: 川菜是中国八大菜系之一。
column5: Sichuan food is one of the eight cuisines of Chinese food.

column3: . . . and so on (sometimes written as a single 等; often used at the end of a sentence)
column4: 有名的景点包括九寨沟、峨眉山等等。
column5: Famous scenic spots include Jiuzhaigou and Mt. Emei and so on.

column3: have done something for quantity up to now; the first 了 indicates the quantity of the action, and the second 了 indicates the action continues to now (so far)
column4: 她已经看了三个小时的电视了。
column5: She has been watching TV for three hours.

column1: S + quantity + 没有 + verb + 了
column3: have NOT done something for quantity
column4: 她三天没有来上课了。
column5: She has not come to class for three days.

column3: 可怕 (awful; dreadful; scary; horrible) is an adjective only, more common in spoken Chinese; 害怕 is similar to 怕 as a verb, can be used alone or taken apart
column4: 这是一个可怕的故事。
column5: This is a terrible story.

column3: literally "back and forth" (e.g., 走来走去), but metaphorically means "over and over again"
column4: 我想来想去,还是决定不去朋友的生日会了。
column5: I thought about it over and over again and decided not to go to my friend's birthday party.
